headline: BNP lawmaker scraps Tk 500 and Tk 1,000 notes to boost bank liquidity
summary: MP AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon proposes withdrawing high-denomination notes to bring hidden cash back into the banking system.
details: BNP lawmaker AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon has proposed scrapping Tk 500 and Tk 1,000 banknotes to increase liquidity in the banking sector and reduce the budget deficit.
The Noakhali-1 MP suggested that people be given two months to deposit these notes in banks and legalise undeclared money by paying a fee of 20 to 25 percent.
Speaking during the budget discussion in parliament, Khokon argued that large amounts of cash are being kept at home because people have lost confidence in the banking system.
He called for a reduction in the number of banks, stating that the sector has been looted and that too many banks currently exist in the country.
The MP claimed that this measure could bring Tk 200 billion to Tk 250 billion back into the system, helping the economy start turning again.
Khokon also highlighted money laundering as a major challenge, urging the government to create a secure financial environment to encourage funds to return from abroad.
He further noted that unemployment and law and order issues are significant hurdles to implementing the proposed budget effectively.
caption:
Should Tk 500 and Tk 1,000 notes be scrapped? A BNP lawmaker proposes a bold move to bring hidden cash back to banks.

BNP lawmaker AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon has proposed scrapping Tk 500 and Tk 1,000 banknotes to increase liquidity in the banking sector and reduce the budget deficit.

The Noakhali-1 MP suggested that people be given two months to deposit these notes in banks and legalise undeclared money by paying a fee of 20 to 25 percent.

Speaking during the budget discussion in parliament, Khokon argued that large amounts of cash are being kept at home because people have lost confidence in the banking system.

He called for a reduction in the number of banks, stating that the sector has been looted and that too many banks currently exist in the country.

The MP claimed that this measure could bring Tk 200 billion to Tk 250 billion back into the system, helping the economy start turning again.

Khokon also highlighted money laundering as a major challenge, urging the government to create a secure financial environment to encourage funds to return from abroad.

He further noted that unemployment and law and order issues are significant hurdles to implementing the proposed budget effectively.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[makes surprise visit to SPARRSO]], calls for modernization
headline: PM Tarique Rahman makes surprise visit to SPARRSO, calls for modernization
summary: The Prime Minister directed officials to transform the space research organization into a modern, self-reliant institution to support national security and development.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman paid a surprise visit to the Bangladesh Space Research and Remote Sensing Organization (SPARRSO) headquarters in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Agargaon, today.
During the visit, the Prime Minister toured various sections of the organization, which operates under the Ministry of Defence, and exchanged views with officers and staff.

SPARRSO Chairman Rashidul Islam briefed the Prime Minister on the organization's overall activities, while officials from different departments presented their ongoing research, innovations, and projects.
The Prime Minister instructed the authorities to develop SPARRSO into a modern, future-ready space research organization capable of supporting the country's development and national security.
He emphasized that the institution should be self-reliant and make meaningful contributions through advanced space science, satellite technology, and remote sensing.
The visit was attended by Defence Adviser Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam, Defence Secretary Md Ashraf Uddin, and other senior officials from the Ministry of Defence and SPARRSO.
